description: Vehicle drivetrain mappings with published light-duty screening priors and transport-service boundaries kept separate.

exergy-imperative-component-methods.title: The Exergy Imperative component accounting methods
exergy-imperative-component-methods.applicable_boundary: Energy delivered to a drivetrain through shaft work at its output
exergy-imperative-component-methods.note: Passenger-kilometres and tonne-kilometres are functional services, not thermodynamic exergy. Performance priors, where present, cite their own sources.

doe-vehicle-efficiency-2024.title: U.S. DOE Fact of the Week 1360: Typical EV efficiency compared with a conventional gasoline vehicle
doe-vehicle-efficiency-2024.license: U.S. Government work; source data credited to DOE and EPA FuelEconomy.gov
doe-vehicle-efficiency-2024.applicable_boundary: Energy stored on a light-duty vehicle to energy used at the wheels on the EPA combined city/highway drive cycle, including net regenerative braking
doe-vehicle-efficiency-2024.note: Charging losses, upstream energy, vehicle-specific behavior, weather, and transport functional units are outside this prior.

nrel-fcev-learning-demonstration-2012.title: NREL National Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle Learning Demonstration Final Report
nrel-fcev-learning-demonstration-2012.license: U.S. Government work; NREL technical report
nrel-fcev-learning-demonstration-2012.applicable_boundary: Hydrogen LHV to net fuel-cell-system electrical output over reported vehicle operating points
nrel-fcev-learning-demonstration-2012.note: Reported net system efficiencies include balance-of-plant loads and span 42%-59% across full- and quarter-power results. A separate DOE/EPA drivetrain range is used only to derive the shaft-output screen.

doe-diesel-technical-primer-2010.title: U.S. DOE Diesel Power: Clean Vehicles for Tomorrow technical primer
doe-diesel-technical-primer-2010.license: U.S. Government work; verify document-specific third-party notices
doe-diesel-technical-primer-2010.applicable_boundary: Fuel chemical energy to useful engine shaft work for then-current diesel and gasoline spark-ignition engines
doe-diesel-technical-primer-2010.note: The primer states 40%-50% for diesel engines and 25%-35% for gasoline spark-ignition engines. These are engine, not tank-to-wheel, ranges.

technology.label: Battery-electric vehicle drivetrain
technology.boundary: Energy discharged from the vehicle battery to net mechanical energy used at the wheels over an EPA combined drive cycle, including regenerative braking; charging and upstream electricity are separate

efficiency.statistic: Midpoint of the DOE/EPA stated typical EV efficiency range
efficiency.range_basis: DOE/EPA stated typical range across the referenced drive-cycle context

applicability.boundary: Onboard stored energy to wheel energy including net regenerative braking; charging excluded
applicability.geography: United States EPA combined city/highway drive-cycle context
applicability.vintage: Source accessed by DOE on 2024-07-10 and published 2024-09-16

efficiency.note: Do not interpret this as wall-to-wheel efficiency or a promise for a specific route, climate, or vehicle.

technology.label: Hydrogen fuel-cell drivetrain
technology.boundary: Hydrogen LHV input to mechanical shaft work; hydrogen production and compression are separate unless included explicitly

efficiency.source_version: NREL/TP-5600-54860 and DOE/EPA 2024 EV drivetrain range
efficiency.statistic: Product of midpoints for reported net fuel-cell-system and typical electric-drivetrain ranges
efficiency.range_basis: Products of the lower and upper source bounds; dependencies are not a statistical confidence interval

applicability.technology: Light-duty PEM fuel-cell system followed by a typical electric drivetrain
applicability.boundary: Onboard hydrogen LHV to mechanical drivetrain output; hydrogen production, delivery, and compression excluded
applicability.geography: United States DOE/NREL vehicle evaluation context
applicability.vintage: 2012 fuel-cell fleet results combined with 2024 drivetrain characterization

efficiency.note: Composite estimate; replace with a vehicle-specific fuel-cell and motor map.

technology.label: Gasoline internal-combustion drivetrain
technology.boundary: Gasoline LHV input to mechanical shaft work; upstream fuel production and road load are separate

efficiency.statistic: Midpoint of the source's gasoline spark-ignition engine range
efficiency.range_basis: Published engine conversion range; not a drive-cycle confidence interval

applicability.boundary: Fuel LHV to useful engine shaft work; transmission, accessories, idle, and road load excluded

efficiency.note: Despite the profile label, this prior stops at engine shaft work; use tank-to-wheel data for a full drivetrain boundary.

technology.label: Diesel internal-combustion drivetrain
technology.boundary: Diesel LHV input to mechanical shaft work; upstream fuel production and road load are separate

efficiency.statistic: Midpoint of the source's diesel-engine range
efficiency.range_basis: Published engine conversion range; not a drive-cycle confidence interval

applicability.boundary: Fuel LHV to useful engine shaft work; transmission, accessories, idle, and road load excluded

efficiency.note: Despite the profile label, this prior stops at engine shaft work; use tank-to-wheel data for a full drivetrain boundary.

metadata.default_policy: selected published F1 priors; explicit vehicle and drive-cycle data preferred
